title: [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois..., pages 650 bis à 787, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This page opens §5, 'Caractérisation universelle de l'enveloppe pro-schématique d'un groupe ...'. The last word of the title is illegible; it may be 'unipotent' or 'abélien'. The section continues the previous pages, where Grothendieck builds an integral 'envelope' of the discrete group Z and of lattices M ≅ Z^n. The previous page computed End^0(Z) ≅ E^1 = Spec(Z + T·Q[T]). This is a commutative affine group scheme over Spec Z. It represents A ↦ {(x_n)_{n≥1} : x_n = m·x_{mn}}, the projective limit of the multiplication-by-m maps on the additive line. Its points are A when A is a Q-algebra and trivial when nA = 0. It thus behaves like G_a over Q and collapses in positive characteristic. This is the integral analogue of the unipotent (Malcev) completion of Z.

This page lays the groundwork for a universal property. Let G be a group scheme locally of finite presentation over a base S.
- A homomorphism of S-group schemes H → G is called unipotent (resp. quasi-unipotent) if it sends the points of H to unipotent (resp. quasi-unipotent) elements of G. Here quasi-unipotent means some power is unipotent. The condition 'can be checked fibre by fibre' over the points of S.
- A homomorphism from a discrete group Γ → G(S) is called unipotent (resp. quasi-unipotent) if the corresponding homomorphism of constant group schemes Γ_S → G is.

The intended statement, prepared on the next page via (57)–(59), is a representability result. The pro-group scheme LEnd_S(𝔊) = LEnd(𝔊) ×_{S_0} S comes by base change from a universal base S_0, which is presumably Spec Z. It receives a canonical map 𝔊_S → LEnd_S(𝔊). For G locally of finite presentation, Hom_{pro-gr/S}(LEnd_S, G) = colim_i Hom(𝔊_{i,S}, G). Composition with the canonical map should identify this with the unipotent (resp. quasi-unipotent) homomorphisms 𝔊_S → G. In other words, the pro-schematic envelope is the universal recipient of unipotent homomorphisms from the discrete group into locally finitely presented group schemes over arbitrary bases. It is constructed once over Spec Z and pulled back.

The problem served is integral and relative unipotent/Malcev completion of discrete groups, in the context of the 'Longue Marche' and Galois/anabelian themes. Quasi-unipotence plausibly points at monodromy representations, whose quasi-unipotence was proved in SGA 7.
errors: No outright error. 'Ce qui se vérifie fibre par fibre' should be read as the definition of unipotent elements for a non-affine, non-flat locally finitely presented group scheme over a general base, not as a theorem. The notion of a unipotent element (e.g. via the closed subgroup it generates in each fibre) is not spelled out on this page.

In positive residue characteristic, unipotent elements of finite type groups have p-power order. The term 'unipotent' therefore mixes different behaviours across fibres; the previous page's E^1 handles this by being trivial in characteristic p. That subtlety is not addressed here.

ideas.what: Unipotent / quasi-unipotent homomorphisms of group schemes over an arbitrary base, defined fibrewise, and for discrete groups via constant group schemes
ideas.usually_credited_to: Quasi-unipotence of monodromy: Grothendieck (SGA 7, ℓ-adic monodromy theorem), Landman, Borel; unipotent group schemes: SGA 3 / Demazure–Gabriel
ideas.where_published: Related notions in SGA 3 and SGA 7 I; this exact relative definition for homomorphisms from discrete groups is not known to me in print

ideas.what: Universal property: the pro-schematic (unipotent) envelope of a discrete group over Spec Z, base-changed to S, corepresents unipotent homomorphisms into locally finitely presented S-group schemes
ideas.modern_name: integral/relative unipotent (Malcev) completion; affine-stack / schematization over Z
ideas.usually_credited_to: Malcev, Quillen (over Q); Deligne (pro-unipotent completions, 1989); over Z: Toën ('schématisation' revisited), Mondal–Reinecke (unipotent homotopy theory over Z)
ideas.where_published: Schematization problem stated in Pursuing Stacks and letters; this specific construction is unpublished as far as I know

missed.claim: Grothendieck sets up a universal characterization of an integral pro-schematic unipotent envelope of a discrete group over Spec Z. Over a field it would be G_a-like, but over Z its building block is Spec(Z+TQ[T]), trivial in characteristic p. It corepresents unipotent (and a quasi-unipotent variant) homomorphisms into arbitrary locally finitely presented S-group schemes. The quasi-unipotent version, which would give a universal 'quasi-unipotent envelope', is not developed on this page.
missed.quote: On dit qu'un hom. de schémas en groupes H → G est unipotent (resp. quasi-unipotent) si l'image des élts de H est un élém. unipotent (resp. quasi unipotent) de G — ce qui se vérifie fibre par fibre.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Integral unipotent completion and integral schematization are active topics (Toën, Mondal–Reinecke, Kubrak–Shuklin–Zakharov). A 'quasi-unipotent envelope' over Z, universal for quasi-unipotent monodromy representations over arbitrary bases, does not seem to be a standard object. It could give a clean target for integral monodromy statements.

deep.surprise_reason: The definitions on this page are routine. The context is a hands-on integral/relative unipotent envelope over Spec Z, with a quasi-unipotent variant designed to have a universal property over arbitrary bases. That is an unpublished and somewhat unusual construction, but it is still preparatory and only sketched.

'l'image des élts de H est un élém. unipotent': the image reads something like 'l'image de H est un élément unipotent' / 'image des éléments de H sont des éléments unipotents'.
